inspection_summary: Inspected all 3,540 Python-split lines of the normalized 1948 Borchsenius–Jessen article. The source develops a continuous semantic chain from ordinary Jensen functions and value distributions, through half-strip generalized almost periodic limits and logarithmic branch-cut corrections, to torus/Fourier density theory for partial Euler products and the resulting mean-motion, zero-frequency, and value-distribution theorems for log zeta and zeta in Re(s)>1/2. Formula OCR is intermittently degraded, but the accepted spans have recoverable mathematical roles from checked prose; dependencies on displayed formulas are explicitly noted.

accepted_units.title: Equidistribution and Euler products as the two initial value-distribution mechanisms
accepted_units.why_material: The introduction separates the classical mean-motion route for trigonometric polynomials from the Euler-product and prime-logarithm independence route for zeta, then identifies generalized almost periodicity as latent structure not used by the older proofs.
accepted_units.context_note: Read as motivation for the later unification, not as a new theorem proved here.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Low; prose carries the comparison despite OCR damage to several formulas and the printed half-plane bound.

accepted_units.title: Fourier density regularity versus Jensen zero-frequency control
accepted_units.why_material: The source juxtaposes Fourier-transform proofs of smooth value densities with convex Jensen functions whose slopes encode mean motion and strip zero frequencies, motivating a bridge between value distribution and zeros.
accepted_units.context_note: The ordinary almost-periodic scope restriction to Re(s)>1 is essential to the later generalization.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Medium; displayed derivative and zero-frequency formulas are OCR-imperfect, but their roles and hypotheses are stated in prose.

accepted_units.title: Program and target conclusions for zeta and log zeta
accepted_units.why_material: The authors state the need to extend Jensen theory to generalized almost periodic functions and preview twice differentiable Jensen functions, density-valued second derivatives, mean motions, strip zero frequencies, smoothness, analyticity, and analogous results for zeta itself.
accepted_units.context_note: This completes the result overview that is truncated in the v1 u01 span at line 129.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Medium; the numerical boundary is OCR-rendered as 89, but the structural claims are clear from the checked prose.

accepted_units.title: Ordinary Jensen functions convert convex slopes into mean motions and zero frequencies
accepted_units.why_material: Definitions of one-sided argument variation support the core package: the mean of log|f| is convex, its one-sided derivatives bound mean motions, derivative differences bound zero frequencies, and differentiability yields exact Jensen formulas; uniform function convergence also gives uniform Jensen convergence.
accepted_units.context_note: The span includes setup needed to interpret left/right motions and the multiplicity convention.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High for exact constants and symbols; prose securely recovers the convexity-to-motion and slope-difference-to-zero-frequency mechanisms.

accepted_units.title: Weak convergence and Fourier decay certify smooth value densities
accepted_units.why_material: The paper fixes the distribution-function convergence notion, parameter continuity, integration over parameters, Fourier-transform uniqueness and convergence, inversion, derivative criteria, and exponential-decay criteria for real-analytic or entire densities.
accepted_units.context_note: This is the reusable measure-theoretic engine invoked repeatedly later.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Medium; several integral displays are degraded, while the convergence and regularity implications remain explicit in prose.

accepted_units.title: Vertical means produce unweighted and derivative-weighted value distributions
accepted_units.why_material: Almost periodicity makes Fourier transforms of empirical value measures converge uniformly on bounded frequency sets, yielding asymptotic distributions both for values and for values weighted by |f'|^2, continuously in the vertical-line parameter.
accepted_units.context_note: The derivative-weighted measure is the later area-formula bridge to zero counting.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Medium; definitions and limiting mechanism are readable, though exact display typography is noisy.

accepted_units.title: The Jensen function is the logarithmic potential of the value distribution
accepted_units.why_material: Truncated logarithms permit passage from empirical value measures to the identity expressing the Jensen function of f-x as the integral of log|u-x| against the asymptotic value distribution.
accepted_units.context_note: The truncation argument handles the logarithmic singularity rather than assuming bounded continuity.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Medium; exact integral notation is OCR-damaged but the limiting identity and truncation rationale are recoverable.

accepted_units.title: Area counting turns weighted value density into Jensen curvature
accepted_units.why_material: The area theorem and Fubini identify an integrated derivative-weighted value distribution with normalized zeros of f-x; convex one-sided derivative inequalities then show that a continuous weighted density forces twice differentiability of the Jensen function, with curvature equal to the density up to the stated constant.
accepted_units.context_note: This is the central conceptual bridge between value distribution and zero frequency.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High for the exact displayed equalities and 2π normalization; the logical chain is explicit in surrounding prose.

accepted_units.title: Half-strip Besicovitch-type mean convergence replaces uniform moving-interval means
accepted_units.why_material: To treat zeta below the ordinary almost-periodic region, the source replaces two-sided uniform interval means by fixed-origin half-line means and defines analytic convergence in mean with arbitrary positive index on reduced half-strips.
accepted_units.context_note: This is a deliberately minimal generalized almost-periodicity interface rather than a full abstract theory.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Medium; the defining formula is partly lost, but fixed-7 limiting semantics and index monotonicity are stated in prose.

accepted_units.title: Generalized limits retain Jensen convexity, mean-motion bounds, zero-frequency bounds, and value distributions
accepted_units.why_material: Theorems 1 and 2 assert that uniform convergence in an inner ordinary strip plus mean convergence on a half-strip yields a uniform Jensen limit, convexity, motion and zero-frequency inequalities, convergence of approximating Jensen functions, and convergence of asymptotic value distributions.
accepted_units.context_note: These theorems are the transfer layer later instantiated with partial Euler products.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High for exact inequalities; theorem prose securely supplies hypotheses and conclusions.

accepted_units.title: Nested rectangles turn mean approximation into local analytic control
accepted_units.why_material: The proof localizes half-strip convergence using nested rectangles: mean convergence controls local sup differences, local maxima have mean values and sublinear growth, and ordinary almost periodicity supplies a uniform nonvanishing point in each window.
accepted_units.context_note: The rectangle constants are technical, but the mean-to-local-control mechanism is reusable.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High for rectangle geometry and estimates; prose and lemma conclusions remain recoverable.

accepted_units.title: Zero, argument-variation, and logarithmic-singularity estimates from one nonvanishing point
accepted_units.why_material: Jensen, Carathéodory, and harmonic estimates bound local zero counts, factorized residual size, argument variation, a well-chosen horizontal derivative, and the error from truncating log|F|, all in terms of local growth.
accepted_units.context_note: Routine derivations are retained as one coherent proof toolkit because later generalized-limit arguments depend on its coupled estimates.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High; formula OCR is substantial, so exact constants require scan verification, while lemma statements and dependencies are readable.

accepted_units.title: Truncated logarithms and corrected convex approximants prove the generalized Jensen theorem
accepted_units.why_material: Uniform control of truncated logarithms first transfers log means from approximants to the limit; local argument bounds make horizontal boundary contributions sublinear, and a small correction makes finite-window Jensen means convex so one-sided derivative limits give motion and zero-frequency bounds.
accepted_units.context_note: This span supplies the proof architecture behind Theorem 1 rather than merely restating it.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High for detailed inequalities; the order of limiting choices and convexity argument are explicit in prose.

accepted_units.title: Mean convergence transfers asymptotic value distributions through Fourier transforms
accepted_units.why_material: A Hölder-type bound on exponential characters converts mean convergence of analytic functions into uniform convergence of empirical Fourier transforms on bounded frequency sets, and hence convergence of asymptotic distributions.
accepted_units.context_note: This closes Theorem 2 and is distinct from the logarithmic distribution argument later.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Medium; some displays are incomplete, but the Fourier convergence implication is clear.

accepted_units.title: Cut-aware one-sided argument variation for branches of log f
accepted_units.why_material: The source constructs a branch domain by horizontal cuts from zeros and defines left/right variation across cut endpoints and zero endpoints by continuation and limits, preserving the one-sided continuity needed for Jensen arguments.
accepted_units.context_note: This repairs the ordinary argument-variation interface before treating log f.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Low; the construction is carried by detailed prose.

accepted_units.title: Branches of logarithms inherit generalized Jensen and value-distribution limits
accepted_units.why_material: Theorems 3 and 4 extend Jensen convexity, motion/zero-frequency bounds, uniform approximation, and asymptotic distributions to branches g=log f under exponential approximants; constancy of the exponential approximants' Jensen functions forces zero frequency of f itself to vanish.
accepted_units.context_note: The cut-domain qualification is essential: zeros of g are counted only where the branch is defined.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High for exact motion inequalities, low for theorem structure and the zero-frequency consequence.

accepted_units.title: Rare cut windows and good logarithmic approximations isolate branch instability
accepted_units.why_material: Zero-frequency zero for f makes windows intersecting branch cuts density-zero; on most remaining windows uniform approximation of f by zero-free exponentials forces the chosen logarithm branch to match the approximating logarithm, while large-log windows also have vanishing density.
accepted_units.context_note: This supplies the good/bad-window decomposition used in the proof of Theorem 3.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High for estimates; the exceptional-set logic and limiting order are clear in the lemma prose.

accepted_units.title: Backlund-style variation bounds control log f despite cuts
accepted_units.why_material: Zero counts for G=log F, real/pure-imaginary crossing counts, horizontal and vertical argument bounds, a good transversal segment, and a bounded log|G| integral provide local control even when branch cuts divide paths.
accepted_units.context_note: The squared-log loss on cut-divided vertical segments is a material feature of the proof.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High; exact inequalities depend on formula recovery, but each lemma's qualitative bound is explicit.

accepted_units.title: Good/bad-window truncation proves convergence of logarithmic Jensen means
accepted_units.why_material: The proof combines truncated-log comparison on good windows with global growth bounds on bad windows, then chooses the large-log threshold, truncation level, and approximation error in sequence to make the Jensen means of g and g_n converge uniformly.
accepted_units.context_note: The ordering of Q, m, and approximation error prevents logarithmic singularities from invalidating mean convergence.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High for the displayed bound; the decomposition and epsilon argument are readable.

accepted_units.title: Loop corrections restore an argument-principle proof across logarithmic cuts
accepted_units.why_material: Each cut contributes a loop variation term; adding its integral to the finite-window Jensen function restores one-sided derivative identities, while the aggregate correction vanishes in mean because cut windows have density zero. Cauchy's theorem then yields the logarithmic motion and zero-frequency bounds.
accepted_units.context_note: This is the structural repair distinguishing Theorem 3 from the ordinary generalized Jensen proof.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High for signs and exact normalizations; the correction mechanism and vanishing estimate are explicit.

accepted_units.title: Rare branch failures still permit asymptotic distributions of logarithms
accepted_units.why_material: On good windows logarithmic branches are uniformly close, and the exceptional windows have vanishing mean density; this controls characteristic functions and transfers asymptotic distributions from almost-periodic logarithmic approximants to the limit branch.
accepted_units.context_note: This completes Theorem 4 independently of Jensen curvature.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Medium; formula fragments are damaged, but the characteristic-function bound and conclusion are clear.

accepted_units.title: Partial Euler products satisfy the generalized hypotheses for zeta and log zeta
accepted_units.why_material: The Euler products and chosen branch domain define finite approximants; ordinary almost periodicity, uniform convergence to the right, and mean-square convergence in Re(s)>1/2 allow Theorems 1–4 to reduce zeta and log-zeta means, zeros, and distributions to finite products followed by a limit.
accepted_units.context_note: The text's OCR renders 1/2 as 89; the role of the boundary is nevertheless consistent throughout the source.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High for the exact half-plane notation and Euler formulas; the transfer argument is explicit.

accepted_units.title: Independent circular summands yield smooth unweighted and derivative-weighted densities
accepted_units.why_material: Theorem 5 formulates two coupled distributions on finite tori—values of sums of analytic circular components and the same values weighted by a derivative-like sum—and gives eventual absolute continuity, arbitrary smoothness, convergence, and uniform convergence of densities under square-summability conditions.
accepted_units.context_note: This abstraction is designed to cover logarithmic Euler factors and their s-derivatives.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High for the power-series and summability formulas; the theorem's density conclusions are readable.

accepted_units.title: Factorized characteristic functions turn small circular summands into density regularity
accepted_units.why_material: Independence factors the unweighted Fourier transform and expands the weighted transform into products with one or two marked factors; local oscillatory estimates give enough inverse-power decay, while summability yields Cauchy convergence uniformly on bounded frequency sets.
accepted_units.context_note: This is the principal analytic engine behind Theorem 5.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High; product indices and constants are OCR-sensitive, but factorization, decay allocation, and convergence are recoverable.

accepted_units.title: Limit characteristic functions retain explicit convergent product expansions
accepted_units.why_material: The finite factorizations pass to absolutely convergent infinite products and marked-factor series for the limiting unweighted and weighted distributions, making later decay and analyticity estimates possible.
accepted_units.context_note: The weighted expansion requires convergence of both first- and second-order coefficient sums.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High; exact summation indices need scan verification, while convergence claims are explicit.

accepted_units.title: Convolution tails give Gaussian-type spatial majorants for densities and derivatives
accepted_units.why_material: Splitting head and tail variables expresses finite densities as convolutions; exponential moment bounds for tail sums make translated tail probabilities rapidly small, yielding Gaussian-type majorants uniformly for densities and their derivatives and passing them to the limit.
accepted_units.context_note: The weighted case uses a second tail measure and a Schwarz bound but follows the same convolution architecture.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High for constants and moment displays; the head-tail/convolution proof is clear.

accepted_units.title: Divergent step lengths make the unweighted limiting density positive everywhere
accepted_units.why_material: When the component radii are summable the value support is bounded; when they diverge, polygonal selection of tail phases reaches every target neighborhood, tail concentration transfers positive mass through convolution, and continuity then forces the limiting density F to be positive at every point.
accepted_units.context_note: This distinguishes full support from mere smoothness or nonnegative density.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Medium; the geometric selection and convolution implication survive OCR damage to estimates.

accepted_units.title: A nondegenerate double representation transfers positivity to the derivative-weighted density
accepted_units.why_material: Two small circular summands are chosen so the same value has two regular phase preimages with distinct derivative weights; inverse-coordinate maps and a Jacobian lower bound prevent cancellation, reducing positivity of the weighted density G to the already-established positivity of an unweighted tail density.
accepted_units.context_note: The proof explicitly treats proportional and nonproportional analytic functions before applying the local change of variables.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High for Jacobians and analytic expansions; the nondegenerate-two-preimage mechanism is stated coherently.

accepted_units.title: Rate of radius decay controls real analyticity versus entire density extension
accepted_units.why_material: Allocating successive small-radius factors in the characteristic-function products produces exponential Fourier decay; geometric-rate radius decay yields local real analyticity, while supergeometric decay permits arbitrarily strong exponential decay and entire extension in the two real coordinates.
accepted_units.context_note: This is a direct frequency-decay-to-spatial-analyticity transfer.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High for the exact limsup rate and constants, but the dichotomy is explicit in Theorem 8 and proof prose.

accepted_units.title: Uniform tail control upgrades distribution convergence to joint parameter regularity
accepted_units.why_material: Theorem 9 shows that uniform decay and uniform summable majorants in a parameter give continuous measure dependence, joint continuity of densities and derivatives, uniform convergence in value and parameter, and uniform spatial majorants.
accepted_units.context_note: This is required because the vertical-line real part later serves as the parameter.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Medium; the theorem and proof strategy are prose-readable.

accepted_units.title: Diverging variance forces the limiting density and all derivatives to vanish uniformly
accepted_units.why_material: When the square-sum diverges at a boundary parameter while remaining convergent inside, the characteristic function tends to zero away from frequency zero under an integrable uniform majorant, so Fourier inversion and dominated convergence give uniform vanishing of the density and its derivatives.
accepted_units.context_note: This is the later source of the Re(s)→1/2 boundary behavior.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High for the product estimate, low for the dominated-convergence mechanism.

accepted_units.title: Logarithmic Euler factors instantiate the abstract smooth-density theory
accepted_units.why_material: Choosing l(z)=-log(1-z), its derivative-weight companion, prime radii, and log-prime frequencies verifies the abstract hypotheses and yields smooth, positive, analytic, parameter-continuous log-Euler-product densities with uniform decay and boundary vanishing.
accepted_units.context_note: This span contains Theorem 11 and the exact mapping from prime Euler factors to Theorems 5–10.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High for prime-power exponents and boundary symbols; theorem conclusions are clear.

accepted_units.title: Exponentiation transports log-value distributions to zeta-value distributions
accepted_units.why_material: The exponential map sends log-value measures to value measures and transforms densities by summing over all logarithms with the Jacobian factor; Gaussian decay makes these periodized sums and all derivatives converge, giving smoothness, positivity away from zero, analyticity after composition, and boundary-weighted vanishing.
accepted_units.context_note: The distinction between unweighted and derivative-weighted Jacobian factors is preserved in Theorem 12.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High for exact density factors and Fourier-series formulas; the pushforward mechanism is explicit.

accepted_units.title: Prime-log independence identifies torus distributions with vertical asymptotic distributions
accepted_units.why_material: Linear independence of log primes makes long vertical averages of continuous functions equal Haar averages on the finite torus; hence the torus measures are exactly the asymptotic value and derivative-weighted distributions of partial Euler products, and their densities give second derivatives of finite-product Jensen functions.
accepted_units.context_note: This is the deterministic bridge from abstract phase variables back to actual vertical motion.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High for Fourier-transform formulas and constants; equidistribution and its consequence are prose-clear.

accepted_units.title: Log-zeta value density is Jensen curvature and determines motions and zero frequencies
accepted_units.why_material: Theorem 13 identifies the asymptotic distribution of log zeta, expresses the Jensen function of log zeta minus x as a logarithmic potential, proves twice differentiability with curvature 2π times the weighted density, and derives exact mean motions and strip zero frequencies by integrating that density; it also records boundary divergence and the conjugate negative-height version.
accepted_units.context_note: This carries v1 u03 and includes its proof and the negative-direction remark.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High for exact constants, branch-domain notation, and large-Re formulas; the theorem's causal chain is readable.

accepted_units.title: Zeta-value density is Jensen curvature and determines motions and zero frequencies
accepted_units.why_material: Theorem 14 gives the parallel statements for zeta minus x: asymptotic distribution, logarithmic-potential Jensen formula, curvature from the weighted zeta-value density, mean motions, and density-integral zero frequencies; its proof uses the exponential pushforward and relates zeta Jensen functions to all logarithmic preimages.
accepted_units.context_note: This carries v1 u04 and includes the boundary-divergence argument and conjugate negative-height version.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High for exact formulas and exceptional cases x=0 or 1; the proof structure and conclusions are explicit.

accepted_units.title: Zeros of zeta-minus-value and log-zeta-minus-value have unbounded normalized totals over the half-plane
accepted_units.why_material: Theorem 15 condenses the boundary growth of Jensen slopes into the conclusion that the normalized number of relevant zeros in Re(s)>1/2 tends to infinity for log zeta minus arbitrary x and zeta minus nonzero x.
accepted_units.context_note: This is a source-level consequence of Theorems 13 and 14, not a Riemann-hypothesis claim.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Medium; the printed half-plane bound is OCR-degraded but the corollary is readable.

v1_context_repairs.reason: The frozen span ends at line 129 in the middle of the introduction's description of the density G_a(x); lines 135–143 complete its smoothness/analyticity properties, positivity condition, analogous zeta result, and the note that the paper includes the needed distribution proofs.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Jensen slope as a universal interface from approximation to zero frequency
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Convex logarithmic means preserve enough structure under generalized mean approximation that their slopes remain the interface to argument motion and strip-zero density even when ordinary almost periodicity fails.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: This is proved only under the source's half-strip analytic continuation, inner-strip uniform convergence, and mean-convergence hypotheses.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Derivative-weighted value density is the local curvature behind zero counts
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: The logarithmic potential of the value distribution becomes twice differentiable because area counting identifies its curvature with a derivative-weighted value density, whose integral across real parts equals zero frequency.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: Exact constants and applicability require the continuous-density and differentiability conditions stated in the source.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Branch defects can be neutralized by sparse-exception and loop-correction mechanisms
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Logarithmic cuts need not destroy Jensen/argument-principle reasoning when cut-intersecting windows have zero mean density and each cut's lost variation is restored by a loop correction whose aggregate vanishes asymptotically.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The mechanism depends on zero-frequency zero for the exponentiated function and the source's controlled cut geometry.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Finite Euler products form a two-stage transfer scaffold
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Partial Euler products first supply ordinary almost-periodic objects whose torus laws are exact by equidistribution, then generalized convergence theorems transfer their Jensen functions and distributions to zeta and log zeta.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The transfer is conditional on the stated mean convergence and branch-domain hypotheses and does not extend automatically beyond Re(s)>1/2.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Fourier factor allocation yields a hierarchy from smoothness to entire density
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Independence factorizes characteristic functions; allocating enough small factors yields polynomial decay and arbitrary smoothness, while quantitative radius decay upgrades this to exponential decay and analytic or entire density extension.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The weighted law requires additional marked-factor summability, and exact decay rates depend on the radius sequence.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Full support and weighted positivity require distinct mechanisms
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Unweighted positivity comes from phase-polygon reachability plus convolution, whereas derivative-weighted positivity additionally needs two regular representations of one value with separated weights to prevent the weight from degenerating.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The arguments use small analytic circular components and divergence of their effective radii; they are not generic positivity theorems for arbitrary sums.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Exponentiation preserves the distribution program but changes singular behavior
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Zeta-value densities are periodized, Jacobian-adjusted pushforwards of log-zeta densities, allowing regularity and curvature results to transfer while creating a distinguished behavior at value zero and multiple logarithmic preimages.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: Boundary statements need the explicit |x|-weights recorded in Theorem 12; unweighted uniform vanishing is false.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Boundary variance collapse drives Jensen growth near the critical-line edge
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: As the log-Euler variance diverges at Re(s)=1/2, pointwise density flattens while the logarithmic-potential/Jensen quantities grow, producing increasing zero frequencies across the full half-plane.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The source establishes asymptotic distribution and zero-frequency consequences in Re(s)>1/2, not any assertion about the location of zeta zeros on the critical line.
